@image kongball_maincpu

0x00000400  kongball_zoom_desc_x  400 horizontal scale descriptors, 16 bytes each: +0..+4 five bytes the sprite builder ORs into the register, +6 the shift, +8 and +0xc pointers to the two tables, which are the blitter's repeat and stall counters written out (registers.yaml: wheelfir_the_scale_tables_are_the_counters)
0x00001d10  kongball_zoom_desc_y  The same 400 descriptors for the vertical axis
0x000289be  kongball_pal_blast    THE palette uploader that actually runs: 219 of the 222 uploads to the RAMDAC, MEASURED with a breakpoint. An UNROLLED loop with a computed jump: it enters at 256-count, so it uploads ANY stretch (index in wf_pal_idx, count in wf_pal_count) from wf_pal_buffer. That is the palette composition by stretches
0x00029986  kongball_pal_accumulate  Composes the palette by ACCUMULATION: it walks wf_pal_delta and ADDS each increment to the buffer's colour, wf_pal_count colours, and takes one step off wf_pal_steps. It is the fade, and it is the reason each colour takes SIX bytes: they are words, so they can accumulate without clipping, and the upload keeps the low byte. Located with a write watchpoint on the buffer, not by reading the disassembly
0x00029a42  kongball_pal_to_black  Zeroes wf_pal_count colours of the buffer (fade to black)
0x00029a68  kongball_pal_to_white  Fills wf_pal_count colours with 0xff00 (fade to white)
0x00030800  kongball_clip         Clip variant for D2 low bits 7 (axes as declared, x forward, y forward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder
0x00030a6e  kongball_clip_xb_yb   Clip variant for D2 low bits 4 (axes as declared, x backward, y backward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder
0x00030b40  kongball_clip_swap    Clip variant for D2 low bits 3 (axes exchanged, x forward, y forward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder's second entry
0x00030dbc  kongball_clip_swap_xb_yb  Clip variant for D2 low bits 0 (axes exchanged, x backward, y backward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder's second entry
0x0003128c  kongball_arm_register  Sprite register builder. It takes the destination in D0/D1, the descriptor size in D4/D5 and the flags field in D2, passes the position through wf_scale_coord and writes the 24 bytes
0x000312f2  kongball_arm_flags    move.w D2,0xa(a1): the instruction that leaves the flags field in the register, with the bit 8s of x and y already mixed in
0x0004b320  kongball_snd_load_song  wheelfir main. Loads a song: seeds the voice register pointers and the two opcodes per channel, resolves the 31+31 sample tables by adding the base to them, clears the state and sets speed 6
0x0004b4c6  kongball_snd_tick     wheelfir main. Sequencer tick, called ONCE per vblank. Accumulator += 500 with overflow at 543; when the tick counter reaches the speed it advances a row, and if not it runs the per-tick effects
0x0004b54a  kongball_snd_effect_tick  wheelfir main. ProTracker per-tick effects: 0 arpeggio, 1 portamento up (limit 113), 2 portamento down (limit 856), A volume slide (clipped 0..64). It only runs if the parameter is != 0
0x0004b6de  kongball_snd_apply_volume  wheelfir main. Translates (channel volume, master volume) into a base for the sub's volume table and writes it into voice register +0x08. Volume 0 -> 0x842 (silence)
0x0004b774  kongball_snd_read_row  wheelfir main. Reads a pattern row: pattern = order[position], address = song + 0x1b8 + pattern*1024 + offset, and calls the cell reader for the four channels. It wraps the offset at 0x400 (64 rows) and advances the position
0x0004b93c  kongball_note_period_table  wheelfir main. Note -> period table, 36 words for notes 1..36, read from the base 0xdac2c indexed by the note, so index 0 is the `rts` that closes the routine before it. It IS ProTracker's period table with finetune 0: 856, 808, 762, ... 120, 113
0x0004bf56  kongball_volume_matrix_table  wheelfir main. A 64x64 byte matrix: index (channel_vol-1) + 64*(master_vol-1), value = the sub's volume table number (0..64). It occupies exactly 0xdb248..0xdc247

@image radendur_maincpu

0x00000400  irq_vblank            Vblank handler (level 3 vector). Besides its own work, at 0x4a0 it does `andi.w #$f8ff,($10,A7)` + `ori.w #$2000,($10,A7)` on the SR SAVED ON THE STACK: it leaves the rte with the MASK AT 0, which lets the blitter IRQ1 in, and at 0x4b2 it installs 0x1f2a as the level 1 handler (the main loop does the same at 0xf216e..0xf2176). When 0x2091ee is set it calls state_advance (0x484); the SR rewrite and the install then run only if 0x20795c is 0. It counts frames at 0x203200/0x2031fc
0x00000506  page_bit_compose_a    lsr#3/andi 0x20/or -> move.b d1,0x700011: the visible page bit
0x00000520  arm_line_counter      Arms the 0x7a0000 line counter (together with 0x538). MEASURED with `RE_RASTERLOG` (switch WITHDRAWN): it writes 1 near the vblank, and the level 5 vector jumps to the trampoline 0x20f908 -> 0x203164
0x0000071c  page_bit_compose_b    Composes the page bit exactly as page_bit_compose_a, inside a level 5 line handler of its own (0x5d0 installs 0x640 as the level 5 operand; the analysis never reaches the bytes there) that adds a cursor at 0x2091ec to the y scroll, re-arms the line counter with 0x10 and returns by its own rte at 0x780; not part of the vblank, which ends at 0x59a. A chain the game never enters: neither 0x5d0 nor 0x71c runs
0x00001f2a  irq_blitter           IRQ L1 handler (blitter), target of the RAM trampoline 0x20f918, which the main loop installs by writing its operand at 0x20f91a. MEASURED 2026-08-03: turning the driver's courtesy IRQ1 off completely, the game does NOT reach the menu at any clock, so the drawing chain does not start itself and that interrupt is indispensable
0x00001f42  irq1_last_blit        Level 1 handler installed by 0x2516 when the list runs out: it fires the blit prepared at 0x209461 and calls 0x22bc, which enqueues the next one or declares the queue empty
0x00001f94  irq1_chain            Level 1 handler of the chain: it writes the blitter registers from the parameter block at 0x209439, fires the blit (0xffff to 0x70001e, at 0x1fd2) and calls 0x23f2 to prepare the next entry. MEASURED: on the balloon screen EVERY blit comes out of this 0x1fd2, one per interrupt
0x00001fe6  irq1_terminal         TERMINAL level 1 handler, and the other half of the mechanism: it does `andi.w #$f8ff,(A7)` + `ori.w #$2100,(A7)` on the stacked SR, so it leaves the rte with the MASK AT 1, which BLOCKS IRQ1. With that the chain stops by itself until the next vblank, without anyone having to deassert anything
0x00002004  blit_program          Dumps ONE 24-byte entry of the drawing list to 0x700000-0x70001e (ptr at 0x209430) and fires with 0x70001e=0xffff. It is the CHAIN's emitter: one IRQ1 = one blit. MEASURED 2026-08-03: at 16 MHz one blit comes out per SCANLINE (the 57 of frame 1200 fall on lines 224..284, one per line); at 8x it is 7-8 per line
0x000022bc  enqueue_next          Prepares the next blit in the queue (0x203514 = cursor, 0x203518 = end). With the two pointers equal the queue is empty and it jumps to 0x23dc
0x000023dc  queue_empty           Queue empty: it lowers the busy flag (0x209460) and installs 0x1fe6 as the level 1 handler, which is the one that closes the chain
0x000023f2  walk_list             Walks the drawing list and prepares the next entry at 0x209439. With the entry at zero (end of list) it jumps to 0x2516
0x00002532  list_finished         End of the drawing list: it lowers the channel flag (0x2091a4 + 16*channel) the main loop waits on, and enqueues the palette job at 0x207988 that the vblank consumes
0x000025a4  exception_handler     Address-error handler, the only ROM vector that points here (0x0c; the bus-error and the unused vectors go to the rte at 0x25a2): saves the frame at 0x20f8f4, fills the RAMDAC with grey, infinite loop at 0x25d4
0x000025dc  boot_init             Boot initialisation called from reset (0xf2040): clears RAM from 0x201000, calls the sound initialiser 0xf24d0, zeroes the RAMDAC, arms the level 5 and level 1 trampolines (0x20f908 -> 0x782, 0x20f918 -> 0x1f2a) and issues four clear blits to 0x700000
0x00002856  mode_clear_blits      The same four clear blits to 0x700000 as boot_init, each followed by a delay loop; called again from the main loop (0xf186a, under FUN_000dfaf4)
0x000d6b12  palette_range_table   The palette ranges palette_range_copy walks: 95 four-byte entries, byte 2 the first colour and byte 3 the count (0 means 256), each entry's data offset held in the first word of the NEXT one (0x8611 - 0x8314 = 3 x 255 closes entry 94). None of the 95 passes colour 256, so no valid index overflows the 768-byte buffer; read as entries, the bytes from index 95 on are RGB data, and several of those would
0x000e2dfe  displaylist_walker    Walks a grid of cell pointers (step 0x20 in x and y), clears bit 0 of each node's first byte and appends (tile id, x, y) word triples to the object list at *0x203510, storing the advanced cursor back; A6 is its link frame (four stack arguments)
0x000e2ed6  palette_range_copy    Copies palette range N of palette_range_table into the buffer at 0x203208: 3 bytes per colour from 0x203208 + 3 x start, skipped when N is the one it copied last (re_pal_range_last). It overflows into the display-list cursors at 0x203508 only for an index outside the table, and the one source of such an index is the environment loop at 0xe15f0 reading one prop past its array. With that loop corrected no index leaves the table, so a relocation of that buffer is a second guard on the same prototype fault and is not part of the fix (retired 2026-09-24)
0x000e5d04  section_dispatch_table  A table of 45 pointers (0xe5d04..0xe5db7) that ends EXACTLY where the code of init_section_and_dispatch begins (0xe5db8), so an index of 45 or more reads instructions and takes them for pointers. MEASURED per section: section 0 asks for 18 and 0 (valid); section 6 asks for 4608, section 9 for 1014, section 10 for -31206, section 12 for 17183 and section 14 for 210, and those FIVE are exactly the ones that blow up before drawing the race. The PC ends up in the unmapped gap (measured: 0x11f598) walking straight ahead until a bus fault enters through 0x25a2, which in this game is an rte: it returns to the instruction that faulted and refaults for ever
0x000e5db8  init_section_and_dispatch  Prepares the section: clears two 1024-word arrays (0x201e64 and 0x202664) and then JUMPS THROUGH THE TABLE without checking the index. It reads `(*(0x201006))->field_0xc4`, multiplies it by 4 and jsrs to section_dispatch_table[index]
0x000ebb84  object_update         Entity logic: a state machine over the struct at *0x201006 (fields 0x62/0x8c/0xa4 off a0) that calls fixed helpers through a register loaded with lea (jsr (a2)/(a3)) and restarts itself with jsr object_update when its state changes. The largest function (6KB)
0x000f2034  reset                 Entry/boot: init + main loop (state machine)
0x000f2132  wait_loop             The main loop, which is a BUSY WAIT on the channel flag. MEASURED with a PC histogram during the race: the CPU spends 64.4% of the frame here at 16 MHz and 95.6% at 8x. It is not drawing, it is waiting
0x000f2210  crash_site            clr.w (a1) with a1=*(0x203510); an odd pointer raises an address error, whose handler 0x25a4 paints the grey screen
0x000f2284  state_advance         Advances the state: stores d0 at 0x207958 and, when the channel flag at 0x2091a4+16*(d0&3) is set, loads 0x209430, 0x2094e8 and 0x20f760 from row d0&3 of the ROM table at 0xf1fd4 and clears 0x20795c, else sets it to 1. Called from the main loop AND from the vblank (race)
0x000f23d6  sound_start_block     A level 5 entry that starts a sound block: sends the 0xffff marker to the subcpu, puts 49 in the sample counter (0x202e86), ARMS THE LINE COUNTER WITH 100 (0x7a0000) and sets bit 13 of 0x20351c, which writes to the control port, then rte. Nothing in the ROM points to it, and the game never enters it: the vblank's own block start (0x520) arms the counter with 1
0x000f243e  re_snd_stream_src     radendur main. Source of the raster handler that emits the burst, copied to RAM 0x203164 (by 0xf2426). It emits 0xA0A0 on iteration 49 and one word of the block on each of the remaining 48, SELF-PATCHING its pointers and erasing what it has sent
@code 0x000f243e  runs from 0x00203164
0x000f2446  sound_streamer_rom    The sample streamer, in ROM; it is copied to RAM (0x203164) so it can SELF-MODIFY. It sends one sample per line to the subcpu latch and advances its pointer by incrementing the OPERAND of its own instructions (0x20319c and 0x2031a6), 49 firings per block. It touches no register, which saves the whole movem in an interrupt that fires once per line. And that is what makes it fragile: overrunning the pointer corrupts instructions, not data
@code 0x000f2446  runs from 0x0020316c
0x00202e86  re_snd_sample_count   radendur main (RAM). The sample counter of the sound block: set to 49 when a block opens (0x530 from the vblank handler, 0xf23de from sound_start_block), decremented once per line by the streamer (0x2031b6, the RAM copy of 0xf246c/0xf2490) and compared against 49 to detect the first entry of a block (0xf2446). Below zero the streamer has overrun its buffer
0x0020351c  re_snd_ctrl_shadow    radendur main (RAM). Shadow of the control port 0x7c0000: the byte copied to the port after every change. Bit 13 is set when a sound block opens (0x548) and bit 12 when it closes (0xf24a0), both cleared together by the andi.w #0xcfff that precedes each, so the line counter, which bit 13 enables, runs only while a block streams; bits 8-10 drive the EEPROM
0x00203606  re_pal_range_last     radendur main (RAM). The palette range palette_range_copy applied last; the copier returns at once when asked for it again. 0xe2c4a writes 0xffff here to force the next copy
0x0020300c  re_snd_block          radendur main (RAM). radendur's 96 command bytes: six 16-byte registers at 0x20300c, 1c, 2c, 3c, 4c, 5c. Exactly the same format as wheelfir's
0x00203164  irq5_streamer_ram     The level 5 handler, copied to RAM by the game. It is a sample streamer that SELF-MODIFIES and re-arms the counter line by line. Its pointers (0x20319c, 0x2031a6) advance +2 per firing and the sample counter 0x202e86 underflows below zero: after about 172 words the pointer walks into the handler's own code and clr.w's it. MEASURED with `RE_SINRASTER` (switch WITHDRAWN) on (the earlier `RE_RASTER` (switch WITHDRAWN) never existed) and no guard: an address error before the menu
0x0020797c  re_pal_start          Read alongside re_pal_arg (0x203206) by the palette probe, which labelled it "start". It is NOT confirmed to be the starting index of the palette upload: that is all that is known about it. It is recorded because the probe that watched it was withdrawn on 2026-08-04 as superseded, and that address appeared NOWHERE else in the tree
0x0020f918  irq1_trampoline       The IRQ1 trampoline in RAM: a `jmp abs.l` whose OPERAND (0x20f91a) the game rewrites to change handler on the fly. Vector 0x64 points here

@image radendur_subcpu,wheelfir_subcpu,pwball_subcpu

0x00000000  sub_rom               ROM code + sound samples (0x000000-0x0fffff)
0x00000400  snd_reset             Sound CPU reset. It masks IRQs, copies 0x554..0x839 (742 bytes) to RAM 0x201060, clears the command buffer 0x201000..0x20105f, initialises the 6 voices (pointer and loop to 0x83a, table 0x4842, step 0x3d09) and falls into a `bra` to itself: all the work happens in IRQ1.
0x00000544  snd_soft_reset_stub   Stacks PC=0x400 and SR=0x2700 and does an `rte`, that is, a soft jump to the reset. NO vector points at it.
0x00000552  snd_rte_stub          A bare `rte` that 252 of the 256 exception vectors point at. The TRACE one (0x024) points at its twin at 0x550.
0x00000554  snd_isr_mixer         The whole mixer, and it is the IRQ1 handler. It is copied to RAM 0x201060 because it SELF-MODIFIES: 24 slots (read opcode, table base, step and loop pointer, for each of the 6 voices) plus the target of the final `jmp`. 742 bytes, byte for byte identical in wheelfir, pwball and radendur.
@code 0x00000554  runs from 0x00201060
0x000005ba  snd_mix_out_l         Dumps the sum of voices 1+3+5 to the left DAC. `move.w d7, 0x700000.l`, a 16-bit word of which the DAC uses the low 10 bits. No saturation and no clipping: the sum of three bytes cannot pass 765, and that is why the DAC is 10 bits.
@code 0x000005ba  runs from 0x002010c6
0x00000626  snd_mix_out_r         Dumps the sum of voices 2+4+6 to the right DAC. `move.w d7, 0x740000.l`. The stereo split is FIXED by register: there is no pan field anywhere.
@code 0x00000626  runs from 0x00201132
0x0000062c  snd_isr_tail_jmp      `jmp (X).l` with X patchable in RAM at 0x20113a: it is the command machine's state pointer. Each tail chains itself by writing the next one there before its `rte`.
@code 0x0000062c  runs from 0x00201138
0x00000632  snd_cmd_idle          Idle state of the command machine: every IRQ compares the latch (0x780000) against 0xffff and, when it arrives, chains to snd_cmd_apply_v12. It is the APPLY token the main CPU sends.
@code 0x00000632  runs from 0x0020113e
0x00000648  snd_cmd_apply_v12     Applies the command registers of voices 1 and 2 from 0x201000. Each register is 16 bytes: +0 sample pointer (0 = leave alone, skips 8), +4 loop pointer, +8 volume table base (0 = leave alone), +12 opcode word (0 = leave alone, skips 4), +14 phase step. Writing +12 also does a `clr.w dN`, that is, it restarts the phase.
@code 0x00000648  runs from 0x00201154
0x000006bc  snd_cmd_apply_v34     The same for voices 3 and 4, reading from 0x201020.
@code 0x000006bc  runs from 0x002011c8
0x00000730  snd_cmd_apply_v56     The same for voices 5 and 6, reading from 0x201040. It chains to snd_cmd_wait_block.
@code 0x00000730  runs from 0x0020123c
0x000007a4  snd_cmd_wait_block    Waits for the 0xa0a0 token in the latch (a new block begins). On arrival it zeroes the HIGH word of d0, which is the reception index, and chains to the receiver.
@code 0x000007a4  runs from 0x002012b0
0x000007c0  snd_cmd_recv_word     Receives ONE word from the latch per interrupt and leaves it at 0x201000 + index; the index lives in d0's high word and advances by 2 up to 0x60 (48 words = 96 bytes = 6 registers of 16). On completing it returns to snd_cmd_idle. The protocol is blind: the sound CPU answers nothing.
@code 0x000007c0  runs from 0x002012cc
0x000007e6  snd_voice_end_v1      End of sample for voice 1: it puts 0x80 (centre, silence) into d7 without going through the table, reloads a1 with the patchable loop pointer (RAM 0x2012f8) and continues at 0x576. It does not restart the phase.
@code 0x000007e6  runs from 0x002012f2
0x000007f4  snd_voice_end_v3      End of sample for voice 3: 0x80 into d0, reload a3 (RAM slot 0x201306) and back to the `add.w d0,d7` at 0x596.
@code 0x000007f4  runs from 0x00201300
0x00000802  snd_voice_end_v5      End of sample for voice 5: 0x80 into d0, reload a5 (RAM slot 0x201314) and back to the `add.w d0,d7` at 0x5b8.
@code 0x00000802  runs from 0x0020130e
0x00000810  snd_voice_end_v2      End of sample for voice 2: 0x80 into d7, reload a2 (RAM slot 0x201322) and continue at 0x5e2.
@code 0x00000810  runs from 0x0020131c
0x0000081e  snd_voice_end_v4      End of sample for voice 4: 0x80 into d0, reload a4 (RAM slot 0x201330) and back to the `add.w d0,d7` at 0x602.
@code 0x0000081e  runs from 0x0020132a
0x0000082c  snd_voice_end_v6      End of sample for voice 6: 0x80 into d0, reload a6 (RAM slot 0x20133e) and back to the `add.w d0,d7` at 0x624.
@code 0x0000082c  runs from 0x00201338
0x0000083a  snd_silence_loop      Silence loop: four 0x80 samples and a 0x00 terminator. With the loop pointer aimed here as well, a voice pointing at this stays off for ever without needing an enable flag. It is the initial state of all six voices.
0x00000842  snd_vol_tables        An array of 65 volume tables of 256 bytes, 0x842..0x4941 (0x4100 bytes). The base of level v is 0x842 + v*0x100 with v = 0..64, and the transform is table_v[i] = 0x80 + trunc((i-128)*v/64) with truncation towards zero. v=0 is silence (all 0x80) and v=64 is the identity. Linear volume in 65 steps of 1/64.
0x00004842  snd_vol_full          Maximum volume table (v=64), which is the identity d[0x4842+i] = i. It is the one the reset puts into all six voices.
0x00004946  snd_samples           Start of the sample data, unsigned 8-bit PCM centred on 0x80 with 0x00 reserved as the terminator. It is exactly where the three games stop being identical: the sound program is common and only the samples change.
0x00200000  sub_ram               RAM (0x200000-0x20ffff)
0x00201000  snd_cmd_buffer        Command buffer in RAM, 96 bytes = 6 registers of 16 (voice 1 at 0x201000, voice 2 at 0x201010, ... voice 6 at 0x201050). The receiver fills it one word per interrupt and the three application tails consume it. The reset clears it entirely.
0x00201060  snd_isr_mixer_ram     The mixer's RAM copy, 0x201060..0x201345. It is the one that executes and the only one that gets patched. Conversion: RAM = 0x201060 + (ROM - 0x554).
0x00201062  snd_v1_opcode         Sub-CPU (RAM). Voice 1's read opcode, patched live: 0x1e11 = `move.b (a1),d7` (with a phase accumulator) or 0x1e19 = `move.b (a1)+,d7` (one sample per IRQ, the octave above). The six are at 0x201062, 0x2010ce, 0x201082, 0x2010ee, 0x2010a4 and 0x201110
0x0020106a  snd_v1_table          Sub-CPU (RAM). Operand of voice 1's `movea.l #imm,a0`: the base of its volume table. The six: 0x20106a, 0x2010d6, 0x20108a, 0x2010f6, 0x2010ac, 0x201118
0x00201074  snd_v1_step           Sub-CPU (RAM). Operand of voice 1's `addi.w`: the phase increment in Hz. The MODULUS (0x3d09 = 15625, the rate of IRQ1) sits at 0x201078 and is NEVER patched
0x0020113a  snd_tail_slot         Operand of the mixer's final `jmp`: the command machine's state pointer. Possible values, all in RAM: 0x20113e (idle), 0x201154 (voices 1-2), 0x2011c8 (voices 3-4), 0x20123c (voices 5-6), 0x2012b0 (awaiting block), 0x2012cc (receiving word).
0x002012f8  snd_v1_reload         Sub-CPU (RAM). Voice 1's loop pointer: operand of the `movea.l` in the end-of-sample epilogue. The six: 0x2012f8, 0x201322, 0x201306, 0x201330, 0x201314, 0x20133e (a1..a6)
0x00700000  ldac                  left DAC (data_w)
0x00740000  rdac                  right DAC (data_w)
0x00780000  soundlatch_r          latch from the main CPU to the sub CPU (reads the main CPU's command)

@image rltennis_maincpu,rltennisa_maincpu

0x00200000  rlt_ram               RAM (0x200000-0x20ffff)

0x00720001  rlt_ramdac_idx        RAMDAC index_w
0x00720003  rlt_ramdac_pal        RAMDAC pal_rw
0x00740000  rlt_snd1              Sample block of DAC 2 (the driver's snd1_w, which stores it in m_data760000)
0x00760000  rlt_snd2              Sample block of DAC 1 (the driver's snd2_w, which stores it in m_data740000)

0x007a0000  rlt_unknown           Read-only at boot (unknown)

@image wheelfir_maincpu

0x00000400  wf_zoom_desc_x        400 horizontal scale descriptors, 16 bytes each: +0..+4 five bytes the sprite builder ORs into the register (0xe4940..0xe4948), +6 the shift, +8 and +0xc pointers to the two tables, which are the blitter's repeat and stall counters written out (registers.yaml: wheelfir_the_scale_tables_are_the_counters)
0x00001d10  wf_zoom_desc_y        The same 400 descriptors for the vertical axis
0x00011832  wf_curtain_desc       ROM descriptor of the erasing curtain: 256x16 of page 2 at (1,0), which read from ROM is index 0 across its 4096 pixels
0x0002105e  wf_pal_highscores     Palette of the High Scores engine screen, in the 68000 ROM: 256 colours of THREE RGB bytes. It is the fade's destination, and the whole chain is PROVEN byte for byte: the 768 bytes here are identical to the palette live on screen on frame 2788, and the sequence appears exactly once in the whole ROM. So nothing of ours touches that screen's colour, and the badly-composed-palette hypothesis is refuted
0x0002285e  wf_track_table        wheelfir main. Per-track record, 0x8c bytes per entry, indexed by 0x20bc6e. +0x18 = song pointer, +0x1c = sample base. The rest of the entry is not identified
0x00079ea8  wf_song_bank          wheelfir main. First song of the bank. Nine consecutive songs with no gap: 0x79ea8, 0x7dc60, 0x80a18, 0x80fd0, 0x86588, 0x8b340, 0x8fcf8, 0x902b0, 0x97068, ending at 0x9b220
0x0009b3da  wf_page_toggle        Once per frame: picks the 0x100 offset and the 0x20 page bit
0x0009b442  wf_main_loop_trigger  The main loop's trigger write (0xffff to 0x70001e), after the wait on 0x201cb8 that the vblank handler sets at 0xdc488 and after the mask is opened at 0x9b43e
0x0009b4a2  wf_build_scroll_table  A 256-iteration loop composing the per-line byte; 0x9b4c8 puts the page bit in
0x0009cc98  wf_car_graphic        In the car screen loop, emits a GRAPHIC with the literal #$17 in D2 (bit 2 set)
0x0009ccc2  wf_car_curtain        The SAME loop, ten instructions later, emits its ERASING CURTAIN with the literal #$1b (bit 3 instead of 2), at y = scroll counter + 0x154. The two instructions together are the proof that the field is deliberate
0x0009cda4  wf_car_table          Table of the eight slices of the presentation car: 8 bytes per entry (counter threshold, x, pointer to the descriptor). The thresholds are the previous slice's x, and the x values drop by 79 and wrap mod 512, so the strip is 632 px over a 512 plane
0x0009ceda  wf_pal_blast          THE palette uploader that actually runs: 219 of the 222 uploads to the RAMDAC, MEASURED with a breakpoint. An UNROLLED loop with a computed jump: it enters at 256-count, so it uploads ANY stretch (index in wf_pal_idx, count in wf_pal_count) from wf_pal_buffer. That is the palette composition by stretches
0x0009de98  wf_pal_accumulate     Composes the palette by ACCUMULATION: it walks wf_pal_delta and ADDS each increment to the buffer's colour, wf_pal_count colours, and takes one step off wf_pal_steps. It is the fade, and it is the reason each colour takes SIX bytes: they are words, so they can accumulate without clipping, and the upload keeps the low byte. Located with a write watchpoint on the buffer, not by reading the disassembly
0x0009df50  wf_pal_to_black       Zeroes wf_pal_count colours of the buffer (fade to black)
0x0009df76  wf_pal_to_white       Fills wf_pal_count colours with 0xff00 (fade to white)
0x000a4462  wf_generate_road_table  Generates the per-line scroll table of the ROAD, 13 segments, from the lowest line to the highest
0x000a492c  wf_port_7c0001        Writes 0xAC and then 0xFF to the low byte of control_and_link (0x7c0001), each followed by 27 calls to the link poll 0xa4962, which reads bit 5 of 0x7c0000. It is 54 bytes and runs once per frame right before the blit burst. Guarded by 0x20bc98: if that is not zero, it does nothing. The reading of the two values as half scanline widths is refuted under control_and_link in registers.yaml
0x000a51d2  wf_link_share_difficulty  wheelfir main. Shares the DIFFICULTY LEVEL between two linked cabinets, then rebuilds the EEPROM settings block and resets. The second cabinet (wf_link_player_number nonzero) receives a byte over the link and stores it into wf_difficulty; the first sends its own
0x000a5d08  wf_highscores_loop    Loop of the HIGH SCORES screen, with its state machine (dispatch by state at (-2,A5), states 0..7+ from 0xa5f24; it starts at 3). READ from the 68000. It loads 0x2105e as the destination palette, asks for 0xf fade steps, and uploads the whole stretch (idx=0, count=256). It is a SECOND COPY of the double buffer and per-line scroll block already known at 0x9b3da
0x000da580  wf_snd_load_song      wheelfir main. Loads a song: seeds the voice register pointers and the two opcodes per channel, resolves the 31+31 sample tables by adding the base to them, clears the state and sets speed 6
0x000da734  wf_snd_tick           wheelfir main. Sequencer tick, called ONCE per vblank. Accumulator += 500 with overflow at 543; when the tick counter reaches the speed it advances a row, and if not it runs the per-tick effects
0x000da7b8  wf_snd_effect_tick    wheelfir main. ProTracker per-tick effects: 0 arpeggio, 1 portamento up (limit 113), 2 portamento down (limit 856), A volume slide (clipped 0..64). It only runs if the parameter is != 0
0x000da94c  wf_snd_apply_volume   wheelfir main. Translates (channel volume, master volume) into a base for the sub's volume table and writes it into voice register +0x08. Volume 0 -> 0x842 (silence)
0x000daa66  wf_snd_read_row       wheelfir main. Reads a pattern row: pattern = order[position], address = song + 0x1b8 + pattern*1024 + offset, and calls the cell reader for the four channels. It wraps the offset at 0x400 (64 rows) and advances the position
0x000dab44  wf_snd_read_cell      wheelfir main. Decodes a 4-byte cell: instrument, note, effect, parameter. The instrument loads volume/start/loop; the note translates to a period and to Hz and arms the voice register, choosing the form with or without postincrement; the effect dispatches B/C/D/F per row
0x000dac76  wf_period_hz_table    wheelfir main. Period -> playback frequency in Hz table, read from the base 0xdab94 indexed by the period. Only periods 113..856 are read, so the table's bytes are 0xdac76..0xdb245 and it ends right where the volume matrix begins; the base itself is the operand of the `lea` at 0xdab92 that loads it, and what lies between is code and wf_note_period_table
0x000dac2e  wf_note_period_table  wheelfir main. Note -> period table, 36 words for notes 1..36, read from the base 0xdac2c indexed by the note, so index 0 is the `rts` that closes the routine before it. It IS ProTracker's period table with finetune 0: 856, 808, 762, ... 120, 113
0x000db248  wf_volume_matrix_table  wheelfir main. A 64x64 byte matrix: index (channel_vol-1) + 64*(master_vol-1), value = the sub's volume table number (0..64). It occupies exactly 0xdb248..0xdc247
0x000e5274  wf_irq_sprite_list    The level-1 (blitter) interrupt handler: walks the sprite list and fires the next blit from it. Nearly every blit comes out of here; the rest come from the fill and clear routines
0x000e6db2  wf_engine_pitch       wheelfir main. Sets voice 5 (register 0x20cde8: read opcode at +12, step at +14) from the field at 0x20692e+0x38: a playback rate in Hz, scaled from that field, plus 16000 or 6000 by the field at +0x3c, capped at 24000, then raised by 6000 more while the flag at +0x20 is set, so up to 30000. Above 15625, the mixer's modulus (snd_v1_step), it writes the rate minus 15625 as the step and the post-increment read opcode (0x101d instead of 0x1015), so the voice takes one sample per interrupt plus the phase-accumulated remainder: the octave trick of snd_v1_opcode. Named for the engine by its use in the race, not by anything the game prints
0x000dc490  wf_snd_commit         wheelfir main. `move.w 0xffff, 0x740000.l` in the vblank: the "apply the block" order. It is one of only TWO reserved words in the protocol
0x000dc49c  wf_snd_enqueue_block  wheelfir main. Stamps 0xA0A0 plus the block's 96 bytes into the raster's per-line table (0x590(a6) = the line 200 slot of the array starting at 0x400(a6)) and CLEARS the source buffer so that whatever was not rewritten travels as zero
0x000dc50a  wf_scroll_frame       Frame start: writes scroll x and sets scroll y to ZERO
0x000dc544  wf_scroll_vblank      Writes word 8's low byte from D0, which it also stores to 0x201cbe, inside the vblank handler (IRQ3, 0xdc340..0xdc59e), once per frame. MEASURED with a per-site write log over an attract cycle: 2982 writes at vpos 247..262, the page bit set in 1430
0x000dc5f6  wf_raster_starts_road  First raster IRQ of the frame: installs the road handler, arms the counter with horizon+1 and advances the table cursor by as many entries
0x000dc61a  wf_page_of_frame      Sets the frame's page by writing the blitter's word 8. It is the ONLY one of that word's four writers that falls on vpos 0..0, once per frame, and it alternates 951/907 over an attract cycle. MEASURED with `WFV2_SITIOS` (switch WITHDRAWN)=1, which records the writes by PC, whether they carried bit 0x20 and which beam line they fell on: that is what finally separates the four physically, because the access mask does not tell them apart (all four write the low byte)
0x000dc624  wf_write_scroll_and_raster  Writes scroll y (word 11, from 0x201cc0) and re-arms the raster counter with 1, installing 0xdc7b0 as the next handler
0x000dc756  wf_stream_scroll_line  Injects each line's control byte (page bit, x and y bit 8) from the scroll table (+0x200) into word 8, once per line over the visible part; the next instructions write the line's x and y bytes. MEASURED with a per-site write log over an attract cycle: 484870 writes at vpos 1..255, the page bit set in 227290
0x000dc75e  wf_raster_walk        Raster handler: walks the table, writes x and then y
0x000dc78a  wf_snd_stream_word    wheelfir main. Stage of the raster chain that emits ONE word of the block to the latch per scanline and advances the pointer. There are three variants with the same instruction: 0xdc74e, 0xdc78a and 0xdc7c6, each at the end of a run of `nop`s the chain jumps into. This one is never entered: no code writes a target inside its run (0xdc774..0xdc788) into the jump at 0x201c8a
0x000dc7c6  wf_raster_band        Handler of the band ABOVE the horizon: pins the scroll at 257, which is the scenery's first row in the plane, that is a stop against its top edge
0x000dc7d0  wf_road_scroll        Writes word 8 as the constant 0x80 (y bit 8 set, page bit ZERO) on each line of the band above the road, then y=1 at 0xdc7d8. MEASURED with a per-site write log over an attract cycle: 10489 writes at vpos 1..53, the page bit zero in all of them. It is the one that made the page look as if it varied per line, and why the boundary moved with the HORIZON: on those lines the page really is zero
0x000e47fe  wf_scale_coord        The REAL scale, not a percentage: (2x + first table[x] - second table[...]) >> shift, with a 16-byte descriptor per scale. Validated against a known answer: 100 gives the identity and 200 gives exactly double
0x000e484e  wf_clip_dispatch      Entry of the software clipper: scales the descriptor's width and height through wf_scale_coord, rejects a zero size, and branches to one of eight variants by the complement of D2's low three bits (bit 0 set: x walks forward; bit 1 set: y walks forward; bit 2 clear: the axes are exchanged). Every variant rejects what lies wholly outside the rectangle wf_clip_x0..wf_clip_y1 and pins to its edge an end that crosses it; when the pinned end is the walk's start, it flips that axis's direction bit and takes the source from its other end, so the walk ends on the edge
0x000e489c  wf_sprite_build_swapped  Second entry of wf_sprite_build, the exit of the four clip variants that exchange the axes; rejects a zero span and joins the builder with the two coordinates the other way round
0x000e48c2  wf_sprite_build       Builds the 24-byte register; derives the bit 8s of x/y into 0x40/0x80
0x000e498a  wf_clip               Clip variant for D2 low bits 7 (axes as declared, x forward, y forward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder
0x000e4a4c  wf_clip_xb            Clip variant for D2 low bits 6 (axes as declared, x backward, y forward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder
0x000e4b16  wf_clip_yb            Clip variant for D2 low bits 5 (axes as declared, x forward, y backward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder
0x000e4be0  wf_clip_xb_yb         Clip variant for D2 low bits 4 (axes as declared, x backward, y backward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder
0x000e4caa  wf_clip_swap          Clip variant for D2 low bits 3 (axes exchanged, x forward, y forward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder's second entry
0x000e4d76  wf_clip_swap_xb       Clip variant for D2 low bits 2 (axes exchanged, x backward, y forward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder's second entry
0x000e4e42  wf_clip_swap_yb       Clip variant for D2 low bits 1 (axes exchanged, x forward, y backward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder's second entry
0x000e4f0e  wf_clip_swap_xb_yb    Clip variant for D2 low bits 0 (axes exchanged, x backward, y backward), one of the eight the clipper entry picks; leaves to the sprite builder's second entry
0x000e4fdc  wf_fill_direct        Opens a window with a 0xffff trigger and streams bytes through the direct write port 0x70000d (0xff runs, then 0x21 zeros). Nothing in the ROM jumps to it, and it never runs
0x000e528a  wf_sprite_case0       The dispatcher's fifth case: tst.w 0x16(a1) and, if the register's mode is ZERO, it goes to 0xe5292..0xe52f0, which writes parameters, arms and fires WITHOUT touching any mode register. It is the NORMAL case: 117740 of 117742 blits in 90 s emulated
0x000e52a8  wf_sprite_reg7        move.w 0xa(a1),0x70000e: copies the sprite register's flags field into the blitter's word 7. Bits 2 and 3 come down through here, the field that separates drawing from erasing
0x000e52f0  wf_fire_case0         The FIRING of the dispatcher's case 0 (0x70001e=0xffff). Almost everything the game draws comes out through it, sprites and backgrounds alike: 117740 of 117742 blits in 90 s emulated, because case 0 is the normal one and touches no mode register. It is the CONTROL address of the traces, with 52527 firings measured in 50 s
0x000e5300  wf_sprite_dispatch    Dispatches on the mode at 0x16(a1) to the four variants
0x000e531c  wf_sprite_null        A 2x2 blit at (0,0) with no mode: it looks like a blitter reset
0x000e539c  wf_sprite_mode1       Writes 0x70001b=0xff and 0x70001c=0xffff (opaque)
0x000e540a  wf_background_fill    Emits the word-14 FILLS of the BACKGROUND plane: the seed is a destination 2 px wide reading a source one pixel across, and what it clears is the STRIP it declares in height, from edge to edge of the plane. MEASURED over 60 s emulated: 256 declaring rows 0..255 and 213 declaring 230..255. Together with wf_sprite_fill it is the mechanism the game clears its planes with
0x000e541a  wf_sprite_mode2       Writes 0x700019=0xff and 0x70001c=0xffff (transparent)
0x000e5488  wf_sprite_fill        Emits the word-14 fills of the SPRITE PLANE: one per frame declaring half a page and alternating (1408 with rows 0..255 and 1228 with 256..511 over 60 s). It is the game's own DOUBLE BUFFER
0x000e5498  wf_sprite_mode3       Writes 0x70001b=0xff (opaque, without the third)
0x000e550e  wf_sprite_mode4       Writes 0x700019=0xff (transparent, without the third)
0x000e5584  wf_arm_register       Sprite register builder. It takes the descriptor in A0 (width +0, height +2), the destination start in D0/D1, the flags in D2 (bit 0 picks the path at 0xe5652) and the scale indices in D3, passes the descriptor SIZE through wf_scale_coord and writes the 24 bytes
0x000e55ea  wf_arm_flags          move.w D2,0xa(a1): the instruction that leaves the flags field in the register, with the bit 8s of x and y already mixed in

0x000e8f4a  wf_pal_upload         Uploads a STRETCH of palette to the BT478: starting index in d0, number of colours in d1, source in a0. Seven call sites; in the attract it runs once, on frame 8. The one that runs on every screen is wf_pal_blast
0x000e8f68  wf_pal_fill           Fills a stretch of palette with a constant value (d2)

0x00200fe5  wf_bar_master_count   Third copy of the bar's countdown, outside the two page structures, with the same values as the page 0 one. It is the only one of the three that does not live inside a structure, so it is probably the master the other two are copied from; that last part is NOT verified
0x00201056  wf_fade_length        Length of the next palette fade, in steps: every screen start writes a constant (1, 3, 8, 0xf, 0x14, 0x19, 0x28); the fade code stores it minus one in wf_pal_steps, and a length of 1 skips the fade
0x00201058  wf_pal_idx            Starting index of the stretch about to be uploaded to the RAMDAC
0x0020105a  wf_pal_count          How many colours the stretch uploads; the uploader enters its unrolled loop at 256-count
0x0020105c  wf_pal_steps          Steps the fade has left; wf_pal_accumulate counts them down
0x0020105e  wf_pal_pending        Request flag; the uploader clears it once served
0x00201064  wf_pal_delta          Second buffer, holding the per-colour INCREMENT that wf_pal_accumulate adds at every step. Same format of six bytes per colour
0x00201664  wf_pal_buffer         Palette buffer in RAM, 256 colours at SIX bytes each (R,G,B as words, only the low byte is read). It is where the palette is COMPOSED before being uploaded
0x00201ac8  wf_line_scroll_table  Per-scanline table: at +0x200 the byte carrying page, scroll bit 8, 0x10
0x00201cbc  wf_horizon            Lines SKIPPED before the road begins, that is, the horizon line. 0xdc652 arms the scanline counter with this value +1 and advances the table pointer by 2*d0 bytes. MEASURED in the race: 1 at the start, 166 on frame 1198, and it swings with the terrain
0x00201cc2  wf_upper_band         Lines of the band ABOVE the road (stage 0xdc7b0). READ at 0xdc3ba: it is 257 - camera_y when the camera drops below 257, and the horizon then rises by as many lines. Sweeping all 1744 frames of the demo, the band runs on 380 of them. On frame 1595 it is its first 40 lines, and 0xdc7d8 writes all of them the same scroll, 257, which is EXACTLY the scenery's first row: a stop put in by hand against the edge of the road strip
0x00201cc8  wf_scroll_source_table  Per-line source table, 256 entries of two words (x, y). It is packed into bytes in wf_line_scroll_table. At the start of a race it is seeded with y = line + 4 (0xdc9c4)
0x00201e8c  wf_vector_raster      RAM vector through which the raster chain's handlers are installed. That is why a breakpoint on a handler's address can give ZERO: the real entry point moves
0x002069aa  wf_horizon_raster_chain  The horizon line the raster chain uses; it comes from the minimum of the 13 segments' high lines, pipelined over two frames (0x2069a2 -> 0x2069a4 -> here)
0x002069b3  wf_bar_count_page0    Countdown governing the High Scores TIME BAR, in byte +5 of the page structure at 0x2069ae. MEASURED by dumping the whole RAM over six frames and keeping the monotonic bytes: it falls 94, 74, 54, 34, 14, 0 in samples 10 frames apart, that is EXACTLY -2 per frame, which is the same clock at which the bar grows (+2 px per frame). On reaching zero the screen changes. With this the timer mechanism is closed end to end: the blit that draws it, its source in ROM (page 0 x=105, flat colour), its geometry (2 px wide anchored to the bottom of the active half) and now the variable that moves it
0x00208f33  wf_bar_count_page1    The same countdown in byte +5 of the other page structure (0x208f2e). It runs 2 out of step with the previous one (92, 72, 52, 32, 12, 0), which is exactly what two pages alternating frame by frame call for
0x0020b4ae  wf_sprite_list_current  Pointer to this frame's sprite list (0x208f2e / 0x2069ae, they alternate)
0x0020b4b2  wf_sprite_list_other  Pointer to the other frame's list; it swaps with the previous one
0x0020b4b6  wf_page_flag          Frame counter; its bit 0 alternates the double buffer (btst at 0x9b3da, and at 0xa5e3c in the High Scores copy). It is PER SCREEN: each loop increments it as a BYTE, and the change of writer falls exactly on the screen change (0xe399a up to frame 2770, 0xa5e22 from 2771). It was located by looking for the ONLY monotonic word among the 65536 bytes of RAM, which is what is left when all you have is the symptom
0x0020b4b8  wf_clip_x0            Screen window, x0 (it is 0)
0x0020b4ba  wf_clip_y0            Screen window, y0 (it is 0)
0x0020b4bc  wf_clip_x1            Screen window, x1 = 0x150 = 336 (0x9b2c4, 0x9bab6); wf_video_reset sets 0x154
0x0020b4be  wf_clip_y1            Screen window, y1 = 0xff = 255
0x0020b4c0  wf_page_yoffset       0x100 or 0: the builder adds it to every sprite's y. (-0x1a,A5)
0x0020b4c2  wf_page_bit           0x20 or 0: it goes into EVERY line's scroll byte at 0x9b4c8, and at 0xa5e04 in the High Scores copy. EXCEPTION READ FROM THE CODE (0xa5e84): in states 7 and 0xd of that state machine the bit is INVERTED (eori.b #0x20). No heuristic based on counting blits can guess an exception like that; it has to be read
0x0020b4d2  wf_double_buffer_on   If it is 0 it forces the offset and the page bit to zero: it turns the double buffer off. (-0x8,A5)
0x0020bc4e  wf_camera_y           The camera's y, which is the scenery scroll at the start of the frame. Measured: camera_y + horizon is 429 or 430 on every frame, so the horizon always falls on the same row of the plane
0x0020bc54  wf_car_scroll         Scroll counter of the presentation car screen. It falls about 7 units per frame; the background x, the firing of each slice and the curtain's row all come out of it
0x0020bc6e  wf_race_class         wheelfir main (RAM). The race class, 0..11, the column of the race clock step table and the environment. Every boot stores the next attract demo class from the table at 0x76f98; a played race stores 0x20bc6c * 3 + the level map cursor
0x0020bc84  wf_difficulty         wheelfir main (RAM). The service menu DIFFICULTY LEVEL, 0 = VERY EASY 1 .. 4 = VERY HARD 5, from the high nibble of EEPROM settings byte 4 (2 in the shipped EEPROM). It selects the race clock step row; the attract demos clear it around their step load, so they run at VERY EASY
0x0020bc98  wf_link_player_number  wheelfir main (RAM). The COMUNICATION page PLAYER NUMBER, 0 = the first cabinet. Every link routine tests it; it picks whether wf_link_share_difficulty sends or receives
0x0020cc24  wf_snd_active         wheelfir main (RAM). The sequencer's switch: if it is 0, wf_snd_tick returns having done nothing. It turns itself off only when the master volume reaches 0
0x0020cc2c  wf_snd_master_volume  wheelfir main (RAM). Overall volume 0..64. 0x20cc2e is the per-row fade step and 0x20cc28 / 0x20cc2a its two limits; on reaching 0 the player switches off and silences the four voices
0x0020cc3c  wf_snd_speed          wheelfir main (RAM). Ticks per row; it starts at 6 (ProTracker's default). Effect F writes its low byte (0x20cc3d) masked to 4 bits: there is a speed but there is NO tempo/BPM
0x0020cc40  wf_snd_song           wheelfir main (RAM). Pointer to the song in progress. The header is: a word with the number of positions, 31 longs of sample start, 31 longs of loop, 31 words of volume, the order list at +0x138 (128 bytes) and 1024-byte patterns at +0x1b8
0x0020cc44  wf_snd_sample_base    wheelfir main (RAM). Base added to the song's sample offsets to give absolute pointers in the SUB's space. It is also the anchor of the two resolved tables: starts at +4 (0x20cc48) and loops at +0x80 (0x20ccc4)
0x0020cd40  wf_snd_channel1       wheelfir main (RAM). Sequencer channel 1 state, 26 bytes (the four at 0x20cd40, 5a, 74, 8e). +0 instrument, +1 note, +2 effect, +3 parameter, +4 start, +8 loop, +0xC note, +0xE volume, +0x10 period, +0x12 voice register, +0x16 indirect opcode, +0x18 postincrement opcode
0x0020cda8  wf_snd_block          wheelfir main (RAM). The 96 command bytes: six 16-byte registers at 0x20cda8, b8, c8, d8, e8, f8. The first four are the sequencer's channels and the last two the effects the game fires
